html:
SMTO-FIL-0043 — A file copy couldn't start and may have left a partial file

GUID: 06d45d15-3e86-4850-855a-99f217bb7345
Slug: file-transfer-setup-failed
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO hit a problem while getting a file copy ready on a Gateway, and it couldn't confirm that it cleaned up afterwards. A hidden, unfinished copy file may still be in the destination folder.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the destination folder exists, its drive has free space, and the Gateway is allowed to write there. Getting a copy ready fails when the Gateway can't create its temporary file in that folder.
  2. Look in the destination folder for a file whose name starts with .smto-transfer- and ends with .partial (it may be hidden), and tell the person who manages the Gateway if you see one. That leftover may not have been removed, and they can confirm it's safe to delete.
  3. Confirm the file you wanted isn't already at the destination, then ask SMTO to copy it again. Checking first avoids replacing or duplicating a file that is already there.

What success looks like

  • The copy finishes, SMTO reports it as verified, and no .partial file is left in the destination folder.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't keep repeating the copy until the folder problem is fixed, since each failed attempt may leave another partial file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Transfer session setup (source_open or destination_begin) raised an exception, and closing the handle, unlinking the newly created .smto-transfer-*.partial stage or releasing pinned parents also failed, so the error was wrapped as transfer_setup_failed with cleanup_complete false.

What this means

  • Transfer setup raised an exception and its cleanup could not be confirmed complete, so the original failure is wrapped with cleanup_complete:false. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Transfer setup raised an exception and its cleanup could not be confirmed complete, so the original failure is wrapped with cleanup_complete:false.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original setup failure and the exact owned stage/handles; this label specifically preserves incomplete cleanup.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway log for the underlying exception chained to transfer_setup_failed, and inspect the destination parent directory for an orphaned .smto-transfer-*.partial stage and leaked handles. Fix the root cause (permissions, disk space, filesystem errors), remove the confirmed orphan, then start a new copy.
  • Inspect and settle the failed setup's owned resources and cleanup state before establishing a new transfer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported recovery accounts for the failed setup and confirms cleanup before new work.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
